newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian wool prices end week slightly down.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian wool prices end week slightly down.

text.p: Australian wool prices declined marginally over the past week at sales held in Sydney and Adelaide, Australian Council of Wool Exporters (ACWE) said in its weekly market report.
A more positive tone on the last day of selling reversed the softening of the market earlier in the week, it said.

The Wool International eastern market indicator finished at 622 cents a kg clean, down two cents for the week, while the western market indicator remained unchanged on 598 cents a kg with no sales in Fremantle this week.
The Australian Wool Exchange (AWEX) northern and southern indices closed at 886 and 856 respectively, representing decreases of 14 and 19 points over the week.
The western index stands at 866 points.
A total of 74,862 bales were offered this week, with a pass-in rate of 8.5 percent.
Exporters felt that the market performed much as expected this week, with no new factors emerging to alter the current balance between supply and demand, ACWE said.
Principal buyers were large topmakers, suggesting a need to keep processing machinery in operation, it said.
With two weeks of auction remaining before a two week recess over Easter, this could inject a positive note to the market next week, the council said.
In the futures market, premiums in the more distant months brought greater selling interest from producers, particularly beyond October 97, pastoral group Wesfarmers Dalgety Ltd said.

Premiums had been partially eroded in recent weeks but prices up to 120 cents above cash market were possible, it said. Auction sales next week are in Sydney, Geelong and Fremantle with a total of 82,300 bales rostered for sale.
